Resolver lands in internal/mapping/resolve.go with internal/corpus as the artifact reader. Text locator is {page, section, section_ordinal, stop_at}; ordinal is mandatory because REVENUES:/EXPENDITURES: each occur twice on p66. Table locator is {ordinal, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid}, and a (page,ordinal) miss is always ErrNotFound -- never a fingerprint search that resolves elsewhere, since ACFR p12/p13 are identical in fingerprint, content hash AND bbox. Ambiguity/not-found list up to 3 candidates with line and context via ErrHint. Proven: 128 values from pp.66-67, 16/16 column totals tie exactly.

CheckTotals asserts per column and is production-callable, not test-only. A label-less part reads its stated totals from the stop_at boundary, which is how p67 prints them ('$' is both the block terminator and the first character of $27,145,882). StatedTotals takes the first maximal run of exactly one-amount-per-column within the anchor's line: maximal because totals labels contain bare numbers, exact because a doubled totals line must fail rather than guess, line-bound because the next row's figures would extend the run. All four p67 fund-group columns tie.

Three renames applied to spine.yaml in the same commit rather than carried as aliases. Departments deliberately excluded -- they are an orthogonal axis (a fact is both Police and Wages & Benefits) and folding them into category would halve every total.

internal/fact. ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|row_label|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, unit-separator joined so component boundaries cannot shift. row_label is in the tuple because row_path is NOT unique within a rule: p127 prints 13 detail lines all classified taxes/property, and taxonomy.yaml is explicit those are a label not a category -- review caught the collision and it is now a test. Excludes amount and any index, so a corrected figure is a modified line and an inserted row renumbers nothing. Order is the specified (doc_id,page,row_path,column_path,rule_id) EXTENDED by (fiscal_year,basis,id): the specified five tie for two columns of one schedule, and a non-total order defeats the sortedness check it exists to enable. Declared omissions do NOT become facts -- absent is not zero -- so the spine is 128 published facts plus 8 declared absences. amount_cents is always as-printed and sign is presentation, never an instruction to negate.

Duplicate of fisc-gxt, filed independently for the same defect within minutes. Fixed there. Note the fix taken differs from the one proposed here: rather than dropping the maximal-run requirement for label-less parts, amountRun now also considers a run's $-PREFIXED prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. That keeps the maximal-run guard on both paths and uses the distinction the document itself draws -- totals rows are $-marked, data rows bare -- instead of trusting blk.End's position.

Fixed: amountRun considers a run's $-prefixed prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. Deliberately additive -- the maximal run is computed and preferred first, so every line that read before reads identically and the new branch can only turn a failure into a success. p67 spine-expenditures now ties its 8 columns; the spine ties 24 of 24. Regression test TestCurrencyMarkedTotalsRunSurvivesAGluedDataRow covers the glued line, a wrong-width $-prefix, and an unchanged bare run.

extract.py rewritten on poppler 24.02.0, stdlib only. All 786 pages re-extracted; byte-identical across runs, locales, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH/PYTHONHASHSEED. Determinism verified by a third party on an independent re-run. schema_version bumped to 2 on both sides after review found that leaving it at 1 made a broken reader SILENT: Open() succeeded, then Page(n) returned ErrNotFound, which corpus.go documents as the normal 'no such page' case. Bumping it surfaced a real latent bug -- corpus.SchemaVersion was validating both the manifest and each table JSON, two independent contracts sharing one constant. poppler has no structured error channel; stderr is captured per invocation and the docstring says plainly that an empty errors list is not a promise every page came out whole.
